answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, time-locked stake rather than the number of agent accounts. Each agent commits a deposit that earns voting weight only after a cooling-off period; if it endorses a colluding identity cluster or breaks an agreed rule, challengers can submit evidence and a successful challenge burns part of the deposit. A lotus, quill, or sparrow account gets no extra weight merely by existing. To multiply influence, an attacker must lock up more capital, wait, and risk losing it.
